name: Arc-flash point light sensor
summary: Light sensor in a switchgear compartment that detects the flash of an internal arc and signals an arc-flash relay.
description: A point light sensor is mounted inside a switchgear compartment, such as a breaker or cable compartment, and detects the intense light of an internal arc. It is wired or fibre-connected to an arc-flash relay that usually also checks for overcurrent before tripping, so light alone from an external source does not cause a trip.

The drawing should show which compartment each sensor watches, because the trip zone depends on it. The symbol does not show sensitivity, field of view or the self-supervision used to detect a disconnected sensor.
readingNotes: Identify the compartment each sensor covers.
Check whether trip needs light plus overcurrent.
drawingChecklist: Show connection to the arc relay
distinction: A point sensor covers one compartment; a fibre loop sensor covers a long area such as a busbar run.
